newsitem.title: UK: DKB economist says next Fed rate move down, not up.
newsitem.headline: DKB economist says next Fed rate move down, not up.

text.p: The next move U.S. interest rates more likely to be lower rather than higher, said Philip Braverman, chief economist at DKB Securities (USA).

The Federal Reserve's policy-making Open Market Committee (FOMC) is more likely to keep rates steady in September and eventually ease rates further in response to subdued inflation and economic growth in the U.S., Braverman said at a presentation in London.

The DKB economist acknowledged market expectations of a Fed rate rise as soon as the September 24 FOMC, but said that the U.S. central bank should cut its Federal funds rate to 5.0 percent by or soon after Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's next Humphrey Hawkins testimony in February.

He sees U.S. GDP slowing to around 2.0 pct in the fourth quarter of this year and further into 1997. Consumer price inflation is expected to slow to 2.5 percent for the rest of this year and into next.
Consumer spending will also moderate as consumer debt problems mount, Braverman said. Housing is beginning a downtrend and business spending is expected to drop along with corporate profits, he said.
Against this sluggish economic backdrop, Braverman sees the dollar improving and the bond yields declining.

"Dollar strength would be a continuing response to the capital market gains potential in U.S. bonds and stocks, reinforced by a decline in U.S. market and official interest rates," said Braverman in his economic outlook.
This could see the dollar, which was trading at 1.5085 marks and 109.84 yen at 1545 GMT, rising to between 1.55 marks and 1.60 marks but only as far as 110 yen.
Bond yields will decline later this year and into 1997, dropping to below 6.0 percent from 7.10 percent today, he said.
